The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 29-11-2019.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 29-11-2019 at about 11.00 a.m. when he was crossing the road near electronic city nice toll, Electronic city, Bengaluru city, at that time, rider of the Honda CB Twister motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-1453 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to accident, petitioner sustained fracture injuries.

Immediately, after the accident,
petitioner was shifted to Vijayashree Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient and then admitted to District hospital, Mandya, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
It is stated that he has spent more than Rs.2 lakhs towards treatment and Rs.1 lakh towards medicine, Rs.1 lakh towards food, attendant and transport and other incidental expenses.

3. It is contended that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Driver and earning Rs.40,000/-p.m. and was also doing milk vending work and used to earn Rs.10,000/-p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do the work as he was doing earlier and lost income.

The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the rider of Honda Panchanga Nagaraju Alias P. Nagaraju vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115037088/

4.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, he placed exparte.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that this respondent is not a proper and necessary party to the above case as the vehicle motor bike bearing No.KA-50-1453 is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
This respondent has not insured the bike covering the petitioner, therefore the petition is liable to be dismissed.
The petitioner with collusion of the police has filed the false police complaint by misusing the Act.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 29-11-2019 at about 11.00 p.m. in the night, Electronic city nice toll, Electronic city, Bengaluru city, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration number:
KA-50-K-1453?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and one Dhanush - MRD department, Bangalore got examined as PW-2 and got marked Ex-P1 and Ex.P10.
Also examined Dr.Mahendrakumar K.L. through court commissioner as CW.1 and got marked Ex.C1 to C6 documents.
The respondents have not led either oral or documentary evidence.
8. Heard the arguments.

sentences.text: Issues No.1:

As per the case of the petitioner, on 29- 11-2019 at about 11.00 a.m. when he was crossing the road near electronic city nice toll, Electronic city, Bengaluru city, at that time, rider of the Honda CB Twister motor cycle bearing No.KA-50- K-1453 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to accident,
petitioner sustained fracture injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove his case, got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, charge sheet, spot Mahazar, statements, IMV report, Wound certificate as per Ex.P1 to 8.
11.

According to the version of petitioner the accident happened near Electronic city nice toll,
Electronic city, Bengaluru city, at that time rider of the said motor cycle rode the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.4 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P4 it reflects that petitioner was crossing the road, rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-1453, came in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the petitioner, due to which petitioner sustained injuries.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the rider of offending vehicle rode it in a normal speed by observing on moving vehicles on the road, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.7 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.

Further more,
even the chargesheet as per Ex.P3 was also filed as against the rider of the motor cycle.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.4 and 7 coupled with Ex.P3 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
12. Even in the instant case, the rider of the motor cycle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50-K-1453 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-50-K-1453.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-50-K-1453.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

sentences.text: Petitioner has also examined two witnesses as PW.2 and CW.1.
PW.2 who is working at M.R.D. Department at Vijayashree Hospitals, has produced MLC register extract and police intimation at Ex.9 and 10.

Further to prove the nature of injuries and the disability suffered by the petitioner, he has examined Dr. Mahendra Kumar K.L. who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at MIMS, Mandya, through court commissioner as CW.1 and he got marked inpatient record, X-rays, Old followup OPD book, Recent OPD book and follow up x-rays are marked as Ex.C1 to C6.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that on examination, petitioner had swelling deformity and abnormal mobility over right leg at his lower 1/3rd region, and tenderness, swelling and restricted movement over left clavicle and shoulder region and multiple abrasion over left and right hands.
X -ray of right leg and left shoulder region revealed that both bones of right leg at his lower 1/3rd and fracture of lateral end of left clavicle.
Petitioner underwent surgery on 09.12.2019 for fixation of both bones of right leg fracture, and fracture was fixed with tibia intra-medullary nail and plate and screw for fibula.
After one week lateral end of clavicle fixation was fixed with hook plate and screws on 16.12.2019.
He was discharged on 19.12.2019 with an advise to take follow up treatment.
In clinical examination done on 01.07.2025 petitioner complains of pain at right leg and doing extensional activation with difficulty in sitting cross legged and squatting and climbing stairs.
He had difficulty in doing over head activities.
He assessed 30% permanent physical disability for right lower limb by considering the reduction in mobility and stability component with additional points.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injury sustained by the petitioner is not in dispute.
The disability caused to the petitioner would affect on her avocation.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to her whole body.

It is specifically urged by the petitioner that, he is a driver by profession and also doing milk vending work and earning Rs.40,000/- per month as salary and Rs.10,000/- from milk vending, and totally he is earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this court.
When such being the case mere self serving and self proclaimed statement given by the petitioner without any string of either documentary or oral evidence cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.
It is trite law that, when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
The next moot question to be considered is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 29.11.2019.
Therefore, Rs.14,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 25 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 29.11.2019.
In order to prove the age, petitioner has not produced any document before the court.
Hence, this court has taken the age mentioned in wound certificate which came into existence immediately after the accident in which age is mentioned as as 25 years.
Hence the petition was aged 25 years of age at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 42 is 18 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (AIR 2009 SC 3104).

Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,62,880/-(Rs.14,000x12x12x18/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
Wound certificate produced at Ex.P8 discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
The Ex.C1 inpatient record of the petitioner at MIMS, Mandya wherein he took treatment in the said hospital from 30.11.2019 to 19.12.2019 as an inpatient.
The Out patient summary at Ex.C3 & 4 reveals that that petitioner has consulted the doctor several times for follow up treatment.

Considering these aspects,
I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has stated that he spent more than Rs.2 lakhs towards treatment and medicine expenses and Rs.1 lakh towards food, attendant and transport and other incidental expenses.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his contention.
Petitioner/PW-1 in his cross examination admitted that he is having BPL card and he took free treatment.

Since the petitioner has not produced any document to prove that he spent amount for medicine, this tribunal is not awarding Panchanga Nagaraju Alias P. Nagaraju vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115037088/
6 compensation under the head medical expenses.

17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of one month, and also took follow treatment as out patient. Certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.30,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.56,000/- (14,000 X 4) under this head.

19. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 25 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out her remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 12% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.25,000/- on this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES :
The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.20,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has to undergo surgery, for which she has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

21. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:

22.
The petitioner is claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondents have denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount(excluding future medical expenses).
23. Liability:
Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-1453.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2 nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,53,880/-(Rupees Five lakhs fifty three thousand eight hundred and eighty only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.5,23,880/- (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 70% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 30% of Panchanga Nagaraju Alias P. towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.
